mods.0: Whether we feel happy or sad, content or discontent, {1|is} not determined merely by each individual successive moment of life experience ― a good thing happens and I’m happy, a bad thing happens and I’m sad.
mods.1: While our experiences affect our mood, we are not {2|blown} in a completely new direction by each gust of wind.
mods.2: As humans, we get used to new information and events, both good and bad, and come back to our own usual level of well-being.
mods.3: There will be highs and lows, but over time, like water seeking its own level, we are {3|pulling} toward our baseline ― back up after bad news and back down after good.
mods.5: This tendency is best {4|seen} with little kids and their toy joy: When they get what they’ve longed for, they believe they will be happy for the rest of their lives.
mods.7: But then the kids ― like adults ― {5|adapt}.

explain: ③ 주어 we가 baseline 쪽으로 ‘끌려가는’ 것이므로 수동태 are pulled가 되어야 한다. pulling은 능동 진행형이라 틀리다.

mods.7: But then the kids, just like adults, get used to it.

summary: People {A} to both good and bad events and return to their usual {B} of happiness.
explain: 좋거나 나쁜 일에 적응(adapt)하여 원래의 기준 수준(level)으로 돌아온다는 것이 글의 요지이다.

mods.2: People adjust to news and events, whether good or bad, and then return to their own normal level of well-being.
mods.5: {A}, we can see this tendency clearly in little kids and their toy joy: When they get what they’ve longed for, they believe they will be happy for the rest of their lives.

explain: (A) 앞의 일반적 경향에 대한 사례(어린아이)를 들므로 For example. (B) 잠시 행복하다고 믿었지만 결국 적응한다는 반전이므로 However.

mods.6: And for the first few minutes of the rest of their lives, they really are.
mods.7: But after a while, the kids, like adults, adapt to what they have.

explain: 주어진 문장의 they are는 앞 문장의 ‘남은 평생 행복할 것이라 믿는다’의 happy를 받으므로 ⑤ 뒤 위치가 알맞고, 뒤의 But then이 반전을 이끈다.

mods.7: In time, the kids ― as adults do ― get used to their new joy and go back to normal.

options: Our mood goes back to its usual level over time, however good or bad an event is.
Little kids believe that one good thing will make them happy for their whole lives, and they are right.
A bad thing blows us in a completely new direction, so we feel sad for a long time.
Adults feel more joy than little kids when they get what they have longed for.
Losing a first love is the best way to find our own level of well-being.
explain: 기쁜 일이든 나쁜 일이든 시간이 지나면 적응하여 원래의 기분 수준으로 돌아온다는 것이 글의 요지이다.

mods.0: Whether we feel happy or sad, content or discontent, is not {1|determined} merely by each individual successive moment of life experience ― a good thing happens and I’m happy, a bad thing happens and I’m sad.
mods.1: While our experiences {2|affect} our mood, we are not blown in a completely new direction by each gust of wind.
mods.2: As human beings, we adjust to both good and bad news and go back to our usual level of happiness.
mods.4: The euphoria of first love {3|grows}, and so does the despair of a break-up.
mods.5: This tendency is best seen with little kids and their toy joy: When they get what they’ve {4|longed} for, they believe they will be {5|happy} for the rest of their lives.

explain: ③ 사랑의 행복감은 시간이 지나면 ‘사라진다(fades)’는 흐름이므로 grows는 문맥에 맞지 않는다.
